text:
[
  {
    "n": 1,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Empirical Heads Probability",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "If a coin is tossed 1000 times and lands on Heads 510 times, calculate the empirical probability of obtaining Heads."
  },
  {
    "n": 2,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Die Toss Sample Spaces",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "Consider the experiment of tossing a die. Determine the sample space if the interest is in the exact face value versus if the interest is solely in whether the outcome is even or odd."
  },
  {
    "n": 3,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Component Lifetime Interval",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "Given the sample space S = {t | t >= 0} representing the life in years of an electronic component, specify the event that the component fails before the end of the fifth year as a subset of S."
  },
  {
    "n": 4,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Intersection of Engineering and Gender",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "Let E be the event that a student selected at random is majoring in engineering, and let F be the event that the student is female. Describe the intersection event E and F."
  },
  {
    "n": 5,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Complement of an Item Subset",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "Given the sample space S = {book, cell phone, mp3, paper, stationery, laptop}, find the complement of the subset A = {book, stationery, laptop, paper}."
  },
  {
    "n": 6,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Mutually Exclusive Television Networks",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "A television service offers programs across eight channels affiliated with ABC, NBC, CBS, education, and sports. Determine whether the events of randomly tuning into an NBC program and a CBS program are mutually exclusive."
  },
  {
    "n": 7,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Union of Discrete Character Sets",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "Given the sets A = {a, b, c} and B = {b, c, d, e}, determine their union A or B."
  },
  {
    "n": 8,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Union of Employee Habits and Numerical Intervals",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "For an employee selected at random, define the union of smoking cigarettes and drinking alcohol. Additionally, find the union of the real intervals M = (3, 9) and N = (5, 12)."
  },
  {
    "n": 9,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "At Least One Head in Two Tosses",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "A balanced coin is tossed twice. Find the probability that at least one head occurs."
  },
  {
    "n": 10,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Outcome Below Four on Loaded Die",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "A die is loaded such that an even number is twice as likely to occur as an odd number. Find the probability that a number less than 4 occurs on a single toss."
  },
  {
    "n": 11,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Union and Intersection on Loaded Die",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "For the loaded die where even numbers have twice the weight of odd numbers, let A be the event of rolling an even number and B be the event of rolling a number divisible by 3. Compute the probabilities P(A or B) and P(A and B)."
  },
  {
    "n": 12,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Class Selection by Major",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "A class consists of 25 industrial, 10 mechanical, 10 electrical, and 8 civil engineering students. If one student is selected at random, find the probability that the student is an industrial engineering major, and the probability that the student is a civil or electrical engineering major."
  },
  {
    "n": 13,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Company Job Offers",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "A graduating student assesses a 0.8 probability of receiving an offer from company A, 0.6 from company B, and 0.5 from both. Calculate the probability that he receives at least one offer from these two companies."
  },
  {
    "n": 14,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Sum of Seven or Eleven on Two Dice",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "Find the probability of obtaining a total score of 7 or 11 when a pair of fair dice is tossed."
  },
  {
    "n": 15,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Automobile Mechanic Daily Workload",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "The probabilities that a mechanic services 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, or at least 8 cars on a given workday are 0.12, 0.19, 0.28, 0.24, 0.10, and 0.07, respectively. Find the probability that he services at least 5 cars on his next workday."
  },
  {
    "n": 16,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Rolling Four on Fair Die",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "Determine the probability of rolling a 4 on a standard, fair six-sided die."
  },
  {
    "n": 17,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Uniform Meeting Interval",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "Alice and Bob arrive independently at a uniformly random time between 12:00 and 13:00, each agreeing to wait for 15 minutes. Find the probability that they meet."
  },
  {
    "n": 18,
    "kind": "Task",
    "title": "Three Tosses Sample Space and Events",
    "source": "Tutorial 2",
    "statement": "A coin is tossed three times. Write down the sample space, define events corresponding to exactly two heads, at least one head, and heads on the first toss, compute their probabilities and intersections, and verify the addition rule."
  },
  {
    "n": 19,
    "kind": "Task",
    "title": "Server Cluster Operations and De Morgan Law",
    "source": "Tutorial 2",
    "statement": "In a cluster of three servers, express the conditions that all servers are up, at least one is down, exactly one is up, and at least two are up using event operations. Prove De Morgan's law for the intersection of the three events."
  },
  {
    "n": 20,
    "kind": "Task",
    "title": "Exam Passing Combinations",
    "source": "Tutorial 2",
    "statement": "A student has a 0.7 probability of passing Calculus, 0.6 of passing Linear Algebra, and 0.5 of passing both. Find the probabilities of passing at least one exam, neither exam, exactly one exam, and Calculus but not Linear Algebra."
  },
  {
    "n": 21,
    "kind": "Task",
    "title": "Inclusion Exclusion on Three Events",
    "source": "Tutorial 2",
    "statement": "Given three events with individual probabilities 0.5, pairwise intersections of 0.3 and 0.2, and triple intersection 0.1, compute the probabilities that at least one, none, at least two, and exactly one of the events occur."
  },
  {
    "n": 22,
    "kind": "Task",
    "title": "Basic Event Probability Calculations",
    "source": "Tutorial 2",
    "statement": "Given P(A) = 0.4, P(B) = 0.5, and P(A or B) = 0.7, determine the intersection probability, complement probabilities, set difference P(A \\ B), and symmetric difference."
  },
  {
    "n": 23,
    "kind": "Task",
    "title": "Defective Item Sampling Without Replacement",
    "source": "Tutorial 2",
    "statement": "A batch of 10 items contains 3 defectives, and 4 items are drawn at random without replacement. Find the probability of drawing zero defectives, exactly one defective, and at least one defective."
  },
  {
    "n": 24,
    "kind": "Task",
    "title": "Meeting Probability and Threshold Waiting Time",
    "source": "Tutorial 2",
    "statement": "Two people arrive uniformly and independently between 12:00 and 13:00, waiting 15 minutes each. Determine their meeting probability, and find the minimum waiting duration required to ensure the meeting probability is at least 0.5."
  },
  {
    "n": 25,
    "kind": "Task",
    "title": "Broken Stick Triangle Condition",
    "source": "Tutorial 2",
    "statement": "A stick of unit length is broken at two independent uniformly distributed points. Find the probability that the three resulting pieces can form a triangle."
  },
  {
    "n": 26,
    "kind": "Task",
    "title": "Probability Measure Axiom Verification",
    "source": "Tutorial 2",
    "statement": "Evaluate four candidate probability functions on a four-element sample space to determine whether each satisfies the probability measure axioms. For the valid assignment, compute probabilities of specified two-element events."
  },
  {
    "n": 27,
    "kind": "Task",
    "title": "Geometric Series Measure on Positive Integers",
    "source": "Tutorial 2",
    "statement": "Determine the normalizing constant c that makes P({k}) = c / 3^k a probability measure on the positive integers, and compute probabilities of even values and {k >= 3}. Determine whether a function assigning 0 to finite sets and 1 to infinite sets satisfies the axioms."
  },
  {
    "n": 28,
    "kind": "Task",
    "title": "Sigma Algebra Verification and Atomic Generation",
    "source": "Tutorial 2",
    "statement": "Determine which of four collections of subsets of a four-element set constitute sigma-algebras and identify the failing properties for those that do not. Construct the minimal sigma-algebra generated by two singletons."
  },
  {
    "n": 29,
    "kind": "Task",
    "title": "Axiom Derivations and Algebra Closure",
    "source": "Tutorial 2",
    "statement": "Derive the empty set probability and event monotonicity directly from Kolmogorov's axioms. Prove that the intersection of two sigma-algebras is a sigma-algebra, and provide a counterexample demonstrating that their union generally is not."
  }
]
